summary:
The sweep behaves correctly when it runs from the main checkout or from any worktree. In a read-only check against the real cache, all 5 entries were kept: the 4 live roots plus swiftpm/. No candidates came up, so nothing would be moved. Worktree paths with spaces or Japanese characters map correctly. A locked worktree whose directory is missing is held. Symlinked children are left alone. A trash command that is missing or fails is reported as a failure, and --hint never moves anything.

There is one real hole. The live set is the `git worktree list` of whatever checkout the script is run from. A separate clone, like the review clones this workflow creates under ~/Library/Caches/NihongoRide-v135-work/, lists only itself. From there the main checkout's root and every idle worktree root show up as orphans. I confirmed this with a real --dry-run from such a clone: it would move typing_app-c6fa6dd9, jovial-bun-349687-27fd7d31 and confident-cori-ddeb03-5c3d4c92 (2.1 GB). The --hint that run_all_gates.sh prints in that clone reports "4 build roots ... map to no live checkout" and points at the command that would move them. The script's own rule is to refuse when the live set is incomplete, and this case can be detected but is not refused.

Two smaller edge cases, both reproduced in temp fixtures:
- build_root.sh uses the shell's built-in `pwd -P`, which keeps the caller's spelling (case and Unicode form). If gates are run through a differently-cased path, the root they build into maps to no live checkout.
- A NihongoRide-build directory that is itself a symlink is followed. The sweep then selects date-named folders (YYYYMMDD is 8 hex digits) in the target directory.

findings.failure_scenario: An agent works in a private clone, as this review workflow tells it to (~/Library/Caches/NihongoRide-v135-work/review-1003/<lens>). It runs run_all_gates.sh there, and the hint says 4 roots map to no live checkout and suggests the sweep. Running `python3 scripts/sweep_build_roots.py` without --dry-run from that clone moves typing_app-c6fa6dd9 (the main checkout's root) and the root of every worktree idle for more than 60 minutes to the Trash. Every live checkout then rebuilds from scratch, and the space stays on disk in the Trash. The same happens from a separate clone under ~/Documents, where the --repo checkout does map into the cache, so not even the own-root signal fires. The docstring's LIMIT paragraph only describes the opposite direction (a clone's own root being swept), so a reader believes running from any checkout is safe. The self-test has no case for running from a clone.
findings.fix: In live_checkouts(), compute root_of() for the --repo checkout's own toplevel first. If it is None, raise SweepError naming the problem: this checkout does not build into the cache, so its worktree list cannot vouch for the roots in it; run from /Users/jason/Documents/typing_app or pass --repo. --hint should then stay silent or say it cannot check from here. To also cover clones under ~/Documents, have run_all_gates.sh record the owning checkout in each root (e.g. `printf '%s\n' "$REPO" > "$root/.checkout"`), and have the sweep keep any root whose recorded checkout is an existing directory. Add a self-test case: a separate `git clone` of the fixture repo, used as --repo, must refuse or select nothing.

verdict.reasoning:
The defect is real; I could not refute it. The severity is lower than claimed: SERIOUS, not BLOCKER.

Mechanism at 22842bb:
- `--repo` defaults to the script's own checkout (line 307), and `run_all_gates.sh` line 339 calls `--hint` with that default.
- `live_checkouts()` builds the live set only from `git worktree list` of that checkout. A separate clone lists only itself, so the main checkout and its worktrees are never counted as live.
- When the clone sits outside ~/Documents, `root_of()` returns None. Lines 144-150 treat that as an "attribute misread" and only hold roots named after the clone. Nothing tells the user that the worktree list came from the wrong repository.
- When the clone sits inside ~/Documents, it maps into the cache normally. No note is printed at all, and the main checkout's and worktrees' roots still become candidates.
- The docstring's LIMIT paragraph covers only the other direction (a clone's root being swept when run from main). The self-test has no case where `--repo` is a separate clone.

Why SERIOUS rather than BLOCKER:
- The setup is plausible. This very review harness puts agents in `git clone --shared` copies under ~/Library/Caches/..., and the project's memory says agents must not share the live tree. From such a clone, `run_all_gates.sh` prints a false hint, and the suggested `--dry-run` confirms the wrong list.
- What gets moved is only SwiftPM scratch for live checkouts. Each root is pure cache (CACHEDIR.TAG, swiftpm/ only). It is moved to the Trash (recoverable), never deleted.
- A root is moved only after 60 idle minutes and only when no process has it open, has it as its working directory, or names it in its arguments. Active builds are protected, and the PROTECTED sibling directories are never in scope.
- The cost is a cold rebuild of the main checkout and of every idle worktree, roughly 0.7 GB and a few minutes each. Disk use roughly doubles for those roots until the owner empties the Trash, which works against the tool's own purpose (the 2026-09-27 disk-full incident).
- No source, corpus or irreplaceable data is touched, and gates are not broken. The one exception is a narrow race: a build that starts in a live checkout between `plan()` and the move could fail for that run.

It is a clear break of the script's central promise ("only what provably belongs to nobody"), in a plausible situation, with a hint that steers a reader to act. That fits SERIOUS. The proposed fix is sound: refuse when the `--repo` checkout does not build into the cache, and add a self-test that uses a clone as `--repo`.

findings.title: build_root.sh hashes the caller's spelling of the path (bash's built-in pwd -P keeps case and NFC/NFD), so a live checkout's real root can map to no live checkout
findings.evidence:
ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd -P)". Measured: `cd casedir && pwd -P` -> 'casedir', `/bin/pwd -P` -> 'CaseDir' (on-disk), and NFC vs NFD input is echoed back unchanged. Temp fixture with a planted File Provider attribute: live worktree '.claude/worktrees/CaseWT', root built the way run_all_gates.sh does it but with the cwd spelled '.claude/worktrees/casewt':
  would move casewt-1ca516a4/  4 KB  no live checkout; last modified 781.4 h ago
The sweep maps the spelling git recorded (CaseWT -> a different hash and basename), so neither the exact-root match nor the hold-by-name rule protects it.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone runs `cd ~/documents/typing_app && bash scripts/run_all_gates.sh`. This works on case-insensitive APFS, and REPO comes from the logical `pwd`. swift test then builds into typing_app-<hash of the lower-case path>. An hour later the sweep calls that root an orphan and moves it to the Trash, and every gate run in between counts it in the hint. The same applies to a cwd spelled in NFD for a directory git recorded in NFC.
findings.fix: Canonicalise with the on-disk spelling: `ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && /bin/pwd -P)"`, or `/bin/realpath`. Both the build and the sweep go through this helper, so both sides change together. Canonically spelled checkouts, including all current ones, keep the same hash.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute the claim. The bug is real and MINOR is the right severity.

Line 46 of scripts/build_root.sh is `ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd -P)"`. That line was there before this range, but the new sweep now depends on it, which is why it matters here. `pwd -P` uses bash's built-in pwd. It resolves symlinks one path component at a time and does not change the case the caller typed. On this machine `/bin/bash -c 'cd /users/jason/documents && pwd -P'` printed `/users/jason/documents`, while `/bin/pwd -P` printed `/Users/jason/Documents`. zsh's own `pwd -P` does fix the case, so the bug only shows up inside the bash helper.

run_all_gates.sh line 79 sets REPO with a logical `pwd`. zsh passes a mistyped `cd ~/documents/typing_app` into $PWD unchanged, and bash keeps it. So the swift test root gets its hash from the lowercase path. The sweep builds its list of live roots from `git worktree list` paths. Git always reports those in the on-disk spelling, even when `--repo` is spelled in lowercase, so the two hashes never match. The rule that keeps roots by name doesn't help either: it only applies when root_of returns None.

I reproduced this end to end in a scratchpad fixture with a planted File Provider attribute. My first fixture sat under a NihongoRide-v135-work path, and the sweep's PROTECTED rule hid the bug there, so I moved the fixture out from under that path.

Why MINOR and not higher:
- It only happens when the cwd is spelled differently from the disk. All current checkouts and agent worktrees use the on-disk spelling, and the NFD case can't happen with the current ASCII paths.
- What gets moved is a cache that the next run rebuilds. Guard 3 (60-minute age) and guard 4 (lsof/ps) stop it from being moved while a build is using it.
- It is moved to the Trash, not deleted.

So the effect is a full rebuild after a cache was wrongly treated as an orphan, plus a wrong hint count. It loses no data.

I also checked the proposed fix (`/bin/pwd -P`). With it, the lowercase spelling maps to the same root as the correct spelling, and the hashes of correctly spelled checkouts don't change.

findings.title: A symlinked NihongoRide-build is followed, so the sweep's scope becomes the symlink's target and date-named folders there are selected
findings.evidence:
build_dir_for() returns os.path.realpath(<cache>/NihongoRide-build). Temp fixture: NihongoRide-build -> a shared directory holding 'photos-20250101/' (YYYYMMDD is 8 hex digits, so it matches ROOT_NAME):

A plain sweep then moves any folder there named '<anything>-<8 hex>', such as dated backups like 'photos-20250101', into the Trash as an 'orphaned root'.
findings.fix: Refuse (SweepError) when the resolved build dir's basename is not 'NihongoRide-build'. That still allows the legitimate link to a dedicated /Volumes/X/NihongoRide-build. Alternatively, refuse whenever the unresolved path is a symlink.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute this, and I reproduced it. At 22842bb, `build_dir_for()` returns `os.path.realpath(<cache>/NihongoRide-build)` (line 91). `classify()` then runs `iterdir()` over that resolved directory and selects every child matching `^(.+)-[0-9a-f]{8}$`. An 8-digit date (YYYYMMDD) is also 8 hex characters, so `photos-20250101` or `Backups-20240615` counts as a root. The symlink check in `classify()` and the "symlinks" exclusion in rule 1 only cover entries inside the build directory. Nothing checks whether `NihongoRide-build` itself is a symlink, or what its target is called.

Fixture with `NihongoRide-build` linked to a general folder:
- The dry-run, `--hint`, and a real run with a stand-in trash command all selected `photos-20250101/` and `Backups-20240615/`, and the real run moved them.
- Both live checkouts were reported as "builds outside the cache" ("0 with a root here"). This happens because `root_of()` passes `NIHONGO_BUILD_CACHE=build_dir.parent`, so `build_root.sh` answers `<target parent>/NihongoRide-build/...`, which never equals the resolved directory. They were still kept through the `held` basename fallback, so no live root was put at risk.

Control: a link to a dedicated target named `NihongoRide-build` mapped both live roots exactly ("2 with a root here"). So the proposed fix (refuse when the resolved basename is not `NihongoRide-build`) would not break the legitimate move-to-another-disk case.

Why MINOR and not higher:
- It needs an unusual setup: the cache linked to a non-dedicated folder. If someone did that, every build root would also land loose in that folder. The documented way to relocate the cache is `NIHONGO_BUILD_CACHE`, and that always produces a directory named `NihongoRide-build`.
- The sweep is opt-in, and the docstring says to run `--dry-run` first. The dry-run and the gate hint both list the false positives by name before anything moves.
- Files go through `trash -s` and can be recovered until the owner empties the Trash.
- The 60-minute age guard and the open-file/process guards still apply.
- The real `~/Library/Caches/NihongoRide-build` is currently a plain directory, not a symlink (checked with `ls -ld`), and `NIHONGO_BUILD_CACHE` is unset. So nothing is exposed today.

Side observation (not part of this claim, no harm found): `PROTECTED.search(str(child))` tests the whole path. A cache whose path contains `NihongoRide-v<N>-work` has every entry reported as "protected name", so the sweep moves nothing. My first fixture showed this, which is why the second one lives in the scratchpad.

summary:
I ran 52 mutants of sweep_build_roots.py (51 in the script plus one in the runner line) against scripts/test_sweep_build_roots.py in a private clone at 22842bb. The test pins the main guarantees well. The test killed every mutant of these: the live-root exclusion, the held-by-name exclusion (locked or outside), the in-use guard (lsof hits, ps hits, the subpath match), the age guard at 0, the root-name rule, files as candidates, --hint falling through to a real sweep, --hint exiting 1, --dry-run treated as a real run, all three exit codes (REFUSED, FAILED, trusting the trash's exit status), dropping -s, an outside root treated as live, ignoring `locked`, and ignoring NIHONGO_BUILD_CACHE.

Two claimed safety properties are not actually pinned:
(1) The age guard is checked only at "0 vs 60 minutes, with the whole tree touched". Four mutants survive: age read from the root's own mtime only, age counted in seconds instead of minutes, a 1-minute default, and --min-age-minutes ignored.
(2) The "refuse when lsof or ps cannot be read" check is tested only with missing binaries. Accepting an lsof or ps that exits 1 with no output survives.

Several guards are never exercised at all, so mutants removing them survive:
- the NIHONGO_BUILD_ROOT strip (under that mutant, the live worktree's root shows "would move")
- the unreadable → skip rule
- the symlink exclusions (the fixture has no symlinks, but every real root has swiftpm/debug -> out/Products/Debug)
- PROTECTED and the scope check before each move (the sibling fixtures are not root-shaped, so widening the scan survives)

I also found one real code gap that the test hides by realpath-ing its temp dir: the ps argv scan only matches the resolved cache prefix. The unmodified test, run with an unresolved $TMPDIR, fails the "named in arguments" check.

No test computes its expected value with the function under test: root names are re-derived independently with hashlib, and the counts are literals. Under the current code the test cannot reach the real ~/Library/Caches or the real Trash.

I wrote an augmented test in my clone (scripts/test_sweep_aug.py). It passes on the unmutated code and kills M08–M13, M17, M29, M30, M34 and M46. The fixes below are taken from it.

The claimed behaviour is real, but its consequence is mostly refuted.

It is real at the byte level.
